gaps.sentence: The rules don't ___ visitors to touch the paintings.
gaps.explanation: allow + object + to-infinitive: allow visitors to touch. (let + bare: let visitors touch.)
can't stand + -ing (also to-infinitive in AmE): can't stand waiting. -ing accepted as standard.

gaps.sentence: He was made ___ for the damage to the rental car.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, 'be made to do' takes the to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: Do you fancy ___ to the cinema tonight?
gaps.explanation: fancy + -ing (informal British): Do you fancy going…?

gaps.sentence: Could you help me ___ these boxes upstairs?
gaps.explanation: help takes a bare infinitive or to-infinitive: help me (to) carry. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: She left the room without ___ goodbye.
My boss won't ___ me take Friday off.
gaps.explanation: let + object + bare infinitive: won't let me take. (allow/permit take to: allow me to take.)

gaps.sentence: I really can't afford ___ on holiday this year.
gaps.explanation: afford takes the to-infinitive: can't afford to go.
